overview: Host John Petrella interviewed land use attorney Harley Racer about several controversial local developments, including the Salem Street rezoning, a proposed methadone clinic, and the Dover Amendment dispute on St. Clair Road.

items.title: Introduction and Professional Background
items.summary: Host John Petrella introduced land use and litigation attorney Harley Racer, who provided an overview of her legal background representing client groups in municipal and land use disputes.

items.title: Salem Street Rezoning Process
items.summary: Racer described the Salem Street corridor rezoning initiative and noted that the process faced neighborhood opposition due to a lack of early public engagement with the local environmental justice community.

items.title: Proposed Methadone Clinic Zoning
items.summary: Racer explained that the Community Development Board removed the "as of right" designation for clinics from the Salem Street zoning changes following local pushback against a proposed methadone clinic.

items.title: Environmental Justice Policies
items.summary: Racer outlined how environmental justice communities are defined by the state based on income, minority population, and English proficiency, adding that Medford has goals in its comprehensive plan to track these policies.

items.title: St. Clair Road Dover Amendment Project
items.summary: Racer discussed the controversy surrounding a former convent on St. Clair Road, where a developer obtained Dover Amendment zoning relief to lease the property to a non-profit domestic violence shelter.

items.title: Citizen Organizing and Local Government Oversight
items.summary: Racer advised residents to monitor board agendas, organize neighborhood resources, and consult legal counsel to ensure local government bodies are following proper administrative procedures.
